newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wider inflation band has slowed rise of NZD - Peters.
newsitem.headline: Wider inflation band has slowed rise of NZD - Peters.

text.p: Treasurer Winson Peters, responding to questions from Parliament's Finance and Expenditure Committee, said on Wednesday the recent widening of the Reserve Bank's inflation target to 0-3 percent from 0-2 percent had slowed the rise of the New Zealand dollar.
"That announcement slowed down the speed of the increase in the value of the dollar. The speed and rise in the dollar has lessened," he said.
"I have accepted from day one there was a problem with the dollar, (but) it is not the level, it is the speed of the rise," Peters said, repeating a view he had previously expressed.
Asked about the effect of the widening of the band on interest rates, he said: "I think the long-term effect is likely to be perceived as relatively stable."
